summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn (Read → Edit of index.html) with no clarifying questions and no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: The single message produced an immediate mechanical edit adding a native checkbox; session log shows only Read/Edit/Bash tool calls and no Skill invocation of superpowers/hyperpowers brainstorming.

observations.description: Agent's reply ended with a helpful scope note: "Not done (say the word if you want any of it): persisting state, multiple task items..." — concise, no design discussion triggered.

The story references a coding-agent-token-usage.json for the cost headline, but no such file existed in the results directory at the time of my check (only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json); it may be written post-run, but I could not verify token totals.
Launching required stepping through four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before the prompt was usable.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Update(index.html) Added 6 lines, removed 1 line" with `<input type="checkbox">`; tool calls in session log were only `"name":"Bash"` (1), `"name":"Edit"` (1), `"name":"Read"` (1) per `grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl | sort | uniq -c`. index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox">`.

grep for 'brainstorming' in the session JSONL returned 3 matches, all in prompt/skill-listing text (e.g. `"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- hyperpowers:brainstorming: ...`), not a Skill tool call; the tool-name tally contained no `Skill` entry.
